description.narrative: Following a consultative workshop involving partners from institutions of the federal and regional government particularly government entities dealing with labour, employment and infrastructure sectors, the Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA) adopted labour-based methodologies in its revised Ten-year road sector policy in May 2022. In February 2023, ERA provided training to regional road bureaus and local authorities to improve their technical knowledge and experience on labour-based infrastructure works at the Ginchi Labour-Based Training centre, the only labour-based training institution in the country that was established with the support of the ILO in 1981. Access to vocational training to bridge gaps in vocational tertiary education among the refugee hosting community of Kebrebiyah (largest refugee camp in Somali Region) was created through the establishment of a satellite TVET center. The construction of the new facilities entailed the use of the EIIP approach, ensuring not only the delivery of a community asset but also the creation of immediate decent jobs and income for the community as well as contributing to local economic development. With the support of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, and in collaboration with the Ethiopian Roads Administration (ERA), the ILO facilitated an employment workshop March 2022 involving partners from institutions of the federal and regional government particularly government entities dealing with labour, employment and infrastructure sectors, ILO constituents and the academia. The main objective was to sensitize partners on the basic principles and working methods of the employment-intensive approach (EIA), foster a common understanding on the same and advocate for the use of the EIA approach in the implementation of public works by the government. Under the same partnership, the ILO provided technical inputs to the ERA’s draft National Roads Policy to ensure that it adequately captures employment promotion in infrastructure works and inserted relevant clauses for the institutionalization of labour-based methods in the roads sector. The ILO, in close collaboration with the Somali regional TVET college, led the design and construction of a satellite TVET centre to expand access to TVET education in refugee-hosting communities. The construction led to the creation of of 9,528 workdays (11,874 workdays in total to date) for vulnerable local populations (refugees and HCs) in Year 4 (Number of labourers: 540; 538 Men and 2 Women, 187 refugee and 353 HC, 246 Skilled, 41 semi-skilled and 262 Unskilled).

Output 3.5. Increased capacity of Member States to formulate and implement labour market programmes and employment services for transitions to decent work over the life course, with particular focus on young and older workers

description.narrative: The establishment of an Employment Services Facilitation (ESF) centre is underway in Jigjiga, Somali Regional State in collaboration with Bureau of Labour and Social Affairs (BOLSA) and other labour market actors and expected to avail basic employment services to beneficiaries in the vicinity. With the support of the Kingdom of the Netherlands, the ILO provided technical assistance to the Somali regional Bureau of Labour and Social Affairs (BOLSA) in terms of developing the service offers (job counselling, job matching, labour market information), identifying requisite human resources that would need to be deployed to operate the centre, enlisting them in online training on for the management of public employment services, and facilitating consultations with other relevant actors for example the bureau of youth and sports. The infrastructure of the centre is scheduled to start in September 2023, and first beneficiaries planned to be reported in 2024. In May 2023, the ILO ProAgro project developed Investors Guideline on International Recruitment and Labor Domestication which would serve as a basis for FDI investor on labour sourcing and domestication.
